newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fiscal outlook improving -- central bank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fiscal outlook improving -- central bank.

text.p: The fiscal situation of all areas of the Brazilian public sector is improving, giving hope that 1996 will end with an operational deficit below 4.0 percent of gross domestic product, said a Central Bank official.
Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, said federal and state governments, as well as state firms, were raising receipts and controlling expenditures.
"The fiscal figures show we are on a trend of improvement," Lopes told reporters. "There is an improvement in all areas of government."
Brazil posted a consolidated operational public sector deficit for the year to end-September of 3.8 percent of GDP, the same as in the January-August period.

The primary result was a 0.03 percent surplus versus a 0.14 percent of GDP deficit in January-August and the Public Sector Borrowing Requirement, or the nominal deficit, for the nine months showed a 5.97 percent of GDP deficit versus a 6.17 percent of GDP deficit.
